description: California defensible-space requirements (PRC 4291), the draft Zone 0 ember-resistant zone pending final adoption, and advisory items from the IBHS Wildfire Prepared Home standard. Every rule cites its source; rules that are not yet law are marked pending_adoption and carry a caveat shown beside the finding.
disclaimer: Groundwork provides educational guidance based on published state and local requirements. It is not an official inspection, a legal determination, or a guarantee of safety, and it does not provide evacuation guidance. Confirm your obligations with your local fire agency.

rules.title: Remove dead and dying vegetation within 30 feet
rules.rationale: Dead grass, shrubs, and branches ignite from embers far more readily than living plants, and they carry fire toward the house.

action.title: Clear dead vegetation within 30 feet of the house
action.detail: Remove dead plants, dried grass, fallen leaves, and dead branches. Living, well-watered plants can stay.

rules.title: Keep the roof clear of leaves and needles
rules.rationale: A roof holding dry needles is the most common way an ember becomes a house fire.

action.title: Clear the roof and gutters
action.detail: Remove accumulated leaves, needles, and other vegetative debris from the roof surface and gutters.

rules.title: Keep limbs 10 feet clear of the chimney
rules.rationale: Branches over a chimney or stovepipe outlet can be ignited directly by escaping sparks.

action.title: Prune limbs within 10 feet of the chimney outlet
action.detail: Remove tree limbs that sit within 10 feet of a chimney or stovepipe outlet.

rules.title: Reduce fuels between 30 and 100 feet
rules.rationale: The outer zone is where a running fire is slowed down before it reaches the defensible space nearer the house.

action.title: Thin and mow the 30-to-100-foot zone
action.detail: Cut annual grasses down, create space between shrubs and trees, and remove ladder fuels that let fire climb into tree canopies.

rules.title: No combustible mulch in the first five feet
rules.rationale: Bark mulch against the foundation holds embers and burns slowly right at the base of the wall.
rules.citation: Draft Zone 0 regulation, 0-5 foot ember-resistant zone
rules.authority: California Board of Forestry and Fire Protection (draft, April 2026)
rules.caveat: Zone 0 is a draft regulation and has not been finally adopted. This is what the published draft would require; it is not an obligation today.

action.title: Replace bark mulch with gravel or stone in the first five feet
action.detail: Swap combustible mulch against the house for gravel, decomposed granite, or bare soil.

rules.title: Nothing planted against the walls
rules.rationale: A shrub touching siding is a direct path from a ground fire to the structure.
rules.citation: Draft Zone 0 regulation, 0-5 foot ember-resistant zone
rules.authority: California Board of Forestry and Fire Protection (draft, April 2026)
rules.caveat: Zone 0 is a draft regulation and has not been finally adopted. This is what the published draft would require; it is not an obligation today.

action.title: Clear vegetation touching the house
action.detail: Remove or relocate plants growing against exterior walls, and keep the first five feet free of living and dead vegetation.

rules.title: No combustible fence attached to the house
rules.rationale: A wooden fence that meets the wall is a wick: fire travels along it and arrives at the structure.
rules.citation: Draft Zone 0 regulation, 0-5 foot ember-resistant zone
rules.authority: California Board of Forestry and Fire Protection (draft, April 2026)
rules.caveat: Zone 0 is a draft regulation and has not been finally adopted. This is what the published draft would require; it is not an obligation today.

action.title: Replace the last five feet of attached fencing with non-combustible material
action.detail: Swap the section of wooden fence that meets the house for metal, or install a metal gate as a break.

rules.title: Keep the space under decks clear
rules.rationale: Stored firewood, furniture, and debris under a deck give embers somewhere to smoulder out of sight.
rules.citation: IBHS Wildfire Prepared Home, base level requirements
rules.authority: Insurance Institute for Business and Home Safety

action.title: Clear everything stored under the deck
action.detail: Move firewood, furniture, and stored material out from under decks and porches, and clear accumulated leaf litter.

rules.title: Screen vents against embers
rules.rationale: Embers drawn through an unscreened vent start a fire inside the walls or attic, where nobody sees it.
rules.citation: IBHS Wildfire Prepared Home, base level requirements
rules.authority: Insurance Institute for Business and Home Safety

action.title: Fit 1/8-inch metal mesh to vents
action.detail: Cover attic and crawlspace vents with 1/8-inch non-combustible metal mesh, or replace them with ember-resistant vents.

rules.title: Keep gutters free of debris
rules.rationale: A gutter full of dry needles holds fire directly against the roof edge.
rules.citation: IBHS Wildfire Prepared Home, base level requirements
rules.authority: Insurance Institute for Business and Home Safety

action.title: Clear the gutters
action.detail: Remove debris from gutters and downspouts, and consider non-combustible gutter covers.

rules.title: Move firewood away from the house
rules.rationale: A woodpile against the wall is a large, dry fuel load in the worst possible place.
rules.citation: IBHS Wildfire Prepared Home, base level requirements
rules.authority: Insurance Institute for Business and Home Safety

action.title: Relocate firewood at least 30 feet from structures
action.detail: Move stacked firewood and lumber out of the first 30 feet, or store it uphill and away from the house.
